title: This Is How You Get Them To Read
author: The Daily Dad
summary: This short Daily Dad reflection argues that parents trying to raise readers are reaching for the wrong tools. Rules and incentives, such as paying a child for every finished book, miss the simplest and most effective form of teaching, which is example. The piece presses fathers with a series of pointed questions about whether their children ever actually see them reading, or hear them talk about books. It clinches the point with an uncomfortable comparison: children picked up their curse words by watching their parents, so they will pick up reading the same way. The lesson is then generalized to health, kindness and hard work, all of which children learn by imitation more than instruction. The final section promotes the Daily Stoic Read to Lead challenge, but the argument stands on its own as a call to model the habits we want to see.
points: The piece treats reward schemes for reading as a substitute for the harder work of being a visible reader at home.
Its sharpest move compares reading to swearing: children learn both by watching what their parents actually do.
It asks parents to supply evidence, not just claims, that books matter, by making them central to the household.
The same modeling principle is extended to health, kindness and work ethic.
quotes: We want our kids to read. We want them to pick up a book instead of an iPad or a phone.
What we don’t do enough is actually the easiest and clearest form of teaching: We don’t provide a good example.
How often do your kids catch you reading? How often do they see you with a book in your hands?
You want them to read, but do you read regularly to them? You tell them books are important, that books are fun, but where is the evidence?
If you want your kids to read more, show them what a reader looks like. Talk to them about books. Make books a central part of your house…and your lives.
And what’s true for books is true for just about anything—being healthy, being kind, being a hard worker.
